From c132fe78ad7b4ce8b5d49a501a15c29d08eeb23a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jun 2022 08:27:23 +0400
Subject: [PATCH] dmaengine: ti: Fix refcount leak in
 ti_dra7_xbar_route_allocate

of_parse_phandle() returns a node pointer with refcount
incremented, we should use of_node_put() on it when not needed anymore.

Add missing of_node_put() in to fix this.

Fixes: ec9bfa1e1a79 ("dmaengine: ti-dma-crossbar: dra7: Use bitops instead of idr")
Signed-off-by: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220605042723.17668-2-linmq006@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Vinod Koul <vkoul@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/dma/ti/dma-crossbar.c b/drivers/dma/ti/dma-crossbar.c
index 71d24fc07c00..e34cfb50d241 100644
--- a/drivers/dma/ti/dma-crossbar.c
+++ b/drivers/dma/ti/dma-crossbar.c
@@ -268,6 +268,7 @@ static void *ti_dra7_xbar_route_allocate(struct of_phandle_args *dma_spec,
 		mutex_unlock(&xbar->mutex);
 		dev_err(&pdev->dev, "Run out of free DMA requests\n");
 		kfree(map);
+		of_node_put(dma_spec->np);
 		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);
 	}
 	set_bit(map->xbar_out, xbar->dma_inuse);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/dma/ti/dma-crossbar.c`**
- Added a call to `of_node_put(dma_spec->np);` right before returning an error pointer (`ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM)`) in the `ti_dra7_xbar_route_allocate` function. This ensures that the reference count of the node pointer obtained from `of_parse_phandle()` is decremented when it is no longer needed, preventing a reference count leak.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a specific issue identified in the code where the reference count of a node pointer was not being properly managed, leading to a potential memory leak. The added line of code ensures that the reference count is decremented when the function encounters an error and needs to return early, thus fixing the bug related to reference count management. This change is directly linked to the previous commit identified by the fix tag, which introduced the use of `of_parse_phandle()` without proper cleanup.
